scope: R141 frozen generic PGO Oracle screen; no router decision

policy.scope: R141 single-profile generic PGO Oracle screen; no router acceptance
policy.primary: For each CPU pair separately, form the equal-weight geometric mean of five mean latency ratios within each block. Both pairs must have four-block median below 0.99 and at least three blocks below 1.
policy.latency_veto: Any of 2 CPU pairs x 2 affinities x 5 lanes x 3 metrics with ratio median above 1.03 and all four blocks above 1 rejects the candidate.
policy.numeric: Individual ratios use exact raw-sample fractions. Geometric means use 60-digit Decimal arithmetic rounded to 30 decimal places before median and strict comparisons.
policy.interpretation: Paired median changes within inclusive plus/minus 1% are unresolved, never equivalence or a clearly material improvement. Equal weights are an engineering choice, not a real traffic mix. CPU is reported only; no wall-minus-CPU cause inference.
policy.stopping: Exactly one frozen profile-use ELF and 240 cases. If either primary fails or any veto fires, stop this PGO direction: no retraining, profile selection, variants, excluded blocks, retries or extra samples to rescue it.
policy.router: A passed screen only permits separate consideration of an independent seven-lane router comparison with exact-PGO correctness and resource gates. No R140 functional, timing or memory result is transferred to PGO.

limitations: CPU pairs are reported separately; concurrent workers share host caches and scheduler resources.
Each subject keeps one daemon for all lanes and affinity conditions within a block.
Absolute paired median <= 1% is unresolved; larger changes are descriptive directions only.
Register and event lanes use real socket protocol but Oracle rankings do not predict router acceptance.
All raw latency samples, CPU snapshots, subject results, and failed executions remain archived.
The archive verifies recorded identities; live ELF/library hashing is asserted by the runner and is not independently repeated by this offline report.
The fixed generic profile-use candidate is measured once; no profile reselection, training retries or extra variants based on screen results.
Five-lane equal weighting is an engineering choice. Primary eligibility must hold separately on both CPU pairs; neither pair is pooled away.
Every mean/p95/p99 lane on both affinities and both CPU pairs is guarded. CPU is fully reported, with no CPU hard gate.

A failed screen stops this PGO direction. A passed screen does not transfer R140 evidence or authorize adoption; independent exact-PGO router correctness, seven-lane timing and resource evidence are required.
